Traditional (Open Trench) Sewer Repair Some sewer issues require a hands-on approach. With traditional open trench sewer repair, our team carefully excavates the affected area to access and replace damaged pipe sections directly. This method is best suited for severely collapsed or misaligned pipes where trenchless repair isn’t possible. We take every precaution to protect your property and complete the project quickly and safely, restoring reliable sewer function as efficiently as possible. After repairs are complete, we ensure the area is properly backfilled and your yard is left clean and secure. Pipe relining — also called Cured-In-Place Pipe (CIPP) — allows us to restore damaged or deteriorated sewer lines without digging up your property. A flexible epoxy liner is inserted into the existing pipe, then inflated and cured to form a new, seamless inner wall. This method effectively seals cracks, corrosion, and minor root intrusion while extending the life of your sewer line. It’s a fast, clean, and long-lasting solution for homeowners who want to avoid excavation and protect landscaping or hardscapes. Pipe bursting is a trenchless replacement method that installs a brand-new sewer line by breaking apart the old pipe from the inside. Using specialized equipment, a bursting head pulls a new high-density polyethylene (HDPE) pipe through the existing path, replacing it entirely without open trenching. This technique is ideal for severely damaged, undersized, or collapsed lines where relining isn’t an option. It provides a durable, modern pipe rated to last for decades — with minimal surface disruption and faster project completion than traditional excavation. Pipe boring — sometimes called directional boring or horizontal drilling — creates a new underground path for pipes without disturbing the surface above. This technique is often used to install new sewer, water, or conduit lines beneath driveways, sidewalks, or landscaped areas. It’s especially valuable when existing utilities or structures make trenching impractical. The result is a precise, clean installation that maintains the integrity of your yard and property while ensuring accurate pipe alignment and long-term reliability. Our video sewer inspections reveal exactly what’s happening underground, allowing us to diagnose issues quickly and accurately. Using high-resolution cameras, we can identify blockages, cracks, root intrusion, or pipe misalignments without any digging. Basics of Air Conditioning Systems Air conditioning systems operate by removing heat and moisture from indoor air, creating a cooler environment. There are several types of AC units commonly used in Seattle: central air conditioning , mini-split systems , and window units . Central AC systems circulate cooled air through a network of ducts, making them effective for larger homes. Mini-split systems provide flexibility with no ductwork, ideal for individual rooms. Window units are a compact solution to cool individual rooms, making it perfect for rooms where central air conditioning isn’t available. Harts does not work on window units because our main focus is whole home comfort. Knowing your system type helps in selecting appropriate services for repairs or replacements. Common AC Unit Challenges in Seattle Seattle’s climate can lead to specific AC challenges. High humidity and occasional heat waves increase the strain on cooling systems. Common issues include: Clogged filters : Dust and allergens decrease efficiency. Refrigerant leaks : Low refrigerant levels hamper cooling performance. Thermostat malfunctions : Inaccurate readings lead to improper cycling. Addressing these challenges promptly ensures your system operates efficiently, prolonging its lifespan and enhancing home comfort. In Seattle’s wet and sometimes unstable soil conditions, air conditioners can become unlevel over time, which can impact their efficiency and longevity. Here’s how an air conditioner may become unlevel, why this is a concern, and what homeowners in Seattle should know. How Does an Air Conditioner Get Unlevel? Soil Erosion: Seattle’s frequent rainfall can cause soil erosion around the base of an outdoor air conditioning unit. Over time, the ground beneath the unit can shift, leading it to tilt or sink unevenly. Improper Installation: If the air conditioner wasn’t installed on a solid, level foundation initially, it may gradually become unlevel. Gravel, dirt, or a poorly built concrete pad can all contribute to instability. Frost Heaving: In colder months, the freeze-thaw cycle can cause the ground to shift. This is known as frost heaving and can lift or tilt the unit as the soil expands and contracts. Why is an Unlevel Air Conditioner Bad? Reduced Efficiency: When an AC unit is unlevel, the compressor, which is the heart of the system, may not work properly. Compressors rely on the refrigerant being evenly distributed, and tilting can lead to imbalanced refrigerant flow, making the unit work harder and reducing its efficiency. Increased Wear and Tear: An unlevel air conditioner puts additional strain on its components, especially the compressor. Over time, this can lead to premature wear, more frequent breakdowns, and expensive repairs. Drainage Issues: Air conditioners produce condensation, which drains away from the unit. If it’s tilted, the water may not drain properly, leading to pooling around the unit. This can cause rust, mold growth, and even electrical damage. Noise and Vibrations: An unlevel AC unit can become noisier, as the imbalance causes increased vibrations. This not only leads to a more unpleasant sound but can also loosen parts, increasing the likelihood of further damage. Seattle's Air Conditioning Experts Why Choose Harts for AC Repair & Maintenance? Types of Air Conditioning Systems At Harts, we offer a wide range of air conditioning systems to suit your specific needs and preferences. Here&#8217;s a breakdown of some of the most popular options: Central air conditioners are a popular choice for cooling entire homes. They consist of an outdoor unit that draws in warm air and cools it using refrigerant. The cooled air is then distributed throughout your home through a network of ducts. Central air conditioners offer efficient, whole-home cooling and are ideal for larger homes or those with multiple stories. Ductless mini-splits are a versatile option for targeted cooling of individual rooms or zones. They feature an outdoor unit and multiple indoor units, often referred to as air handlers. Each indoor unit can be controlled independently, allowing you to customize the temperature in different areas of your home. Ductless mini-splits are a great choice for homes without existing ductwork or for those seeking to cool specific spaces without affecting the entire house. In some cases, a hybrid system that combines the features of central air conditioning and ductless mini-splits can be a beneficial option for cooling and heating your home . These systems offer the efficiency of central air conditioning for whole-home cooling while also providing the flexibility of ductless mini-splits for targeted cooling. Common Air Conditioning System Issues in Tacoma AC systems in Tacoma, Washington are more prone to excess moisture which can significantly affect the performance and longevity of an air conditioning unit. Tacoma&#8217;s climate can a number of issues that requires preventative maintenance: 1. Increased Humidity Strain In areas with high moisture or humidity, the air conditioning unit has to work harder to remove moisture from the air in addition to cooling. This extra load can strain the system, especially if it’s not properly sized or maintained for high humidity environments. Over time, this can lead to wear and tear on components like the compressor and evaporator coils. 2. Condensate Drain Line Clogging Excess moisture means the AC will generate more condensate, which needs to be drained properly. When moisture levels are high, the condensate drain line is more likely to become clogged with dirt, debris, or algae growth, causing water to back up into the system. This can lead to water damage, mold growth, or system shutdowns. 3. Frozen Evaporator Coils Excess moisture can also cause the evaporator coils to freeze if airflow is restricted or refrigerant levels are low. Frozen coils prevent the system from cooling effectively and may cause the AC to short cycle or completely shut down. 4. Mold and Mildew Growth High moisture levels can encourage the growth of mold and mildew inside the air conditioning system, particularly in the ducts, evaporator coils, and around the condensate pan. Mold spores can then circulate through the home, leading to poor indoor air quality and potential health issues for occupants. 5. Corrosion of Metal Components Moist air can lead to condensation forming on metal components within the AC unit, such as the coils, fans, and other parts. Over time, this excess moisture can lead to rust and corrosion, reducing the efficiency of the system and potentially causing parts to fail prematurely. 6. Reduced Cooling Efficiency Air conditioners are designed to not only cool the air but also remove moisture. When there is excessive humidity in the environment, the AC’s cooling efficiency decreases because the system must expend extra energy to dehumidify the air before it can cool the home effectively. This increases energy consumption and utility bills. 7. Increased Wear and Tear As the AC unit works harder to remove both heat and moisture from the air, it experiences more wear and tear. This added strain can reduce the lifespan of the system and lead to more frequent repairs if maintenance isn’t kept up. How to Mitigate Common Issues: Regular Maintenance : Routine maintenance ensures that your system is clean, has adequate airflow, and the condensate drain line is clear. Dehumidifiers : In areas with extremely high humidity, using a whole-home dehumidifier can reduce the burden on the air conditioning system. Proper Sizing : Make sure your AC unit is properly sized for your home and the climate. An oversized or undersized unit can struggle to handle excess moisture. Check for Mold : Regularly inspect the system for mold or mildew growth and have it professionally cleaned if necessary. In summary, excess moisture can cause multiple issues for your air conditioning system, leading to reduced efficiency, potential water damage, and increased wear. Proper maintenance and climate-specific solutions can help mitigate these challenges. Save On Drain Cleaning & Clearing Signs You Need Professional Drain Cleaning Drain problems rarely happen suddenly. In most cases, your plumbing system shows early warning signs before a complete blockage develops. Recognizing these symptoms early can help you avoid water damage, emergency repairs, and costly sewer backups. Slow Draining Sinks or Tubs If water lingers in your sink, shower, or bathtub before draining, buildup is likely restricting flow inside the pipe. Grease, soap residue, and everyday debris gradually narrow the interior of the drain line, eventually leading to a full blockage if not addressed. Recurring Clogs in the Same Fixture If you’re clearing the same drain repeatedly, the obstruction likely extends deeper within the line. Store-bought solutions may offer temporary relief, but professional drain cleaning removes the buildup completely to prevent repeat clogs. Multiple Drains Backing Up at Once When multiple fixtures are draining slowly or backing up at the same time, the issue may be located in the main sewer line. This is a strong indicator that professional service is needed to restore proper system flow and prevent wastewater from backing up into your home. Gurgling Sounds from Drains or Toilets Unusual bubbling or gurgling noises often signal trapped air caused by a developing blockage. These sounds indicate restricted drainage and should be evaluated before pressure builds inside the line and worsens the problem. Foul Odors Coming from Drains Persistent sewer smells or unpleasant odors can indicate organic buildup or a partial blockage inside the pipe. Professional cleaning removes trapped debris and restores proper airflow within the drainage system. Standing Water Around Floor Drains Water pooling in basements, garages, or laundry areas may signal a blocked floor drain or main line issue. Addressing the problem quickly helps prevent structural damage, moisture intrusion, and potential mold growth. Schedule Your Video Inspection Appointment near Tacoma Today Tacoma Sewer & Drain Services Effective & Noninvasive Sewer Camera Inspection Services Minimize the possibility of expensive repairs and damage in the future with a video inspection of your sewer line and drain pipes. A good rule of thumb is that, if your house was built before 1980 and the sewer pipes have not been replaced, they probably need to get changed out. A sewer line camera inspection is the most effective and thorough method of discovering the condition of your sewer pipes. Harts Plumbers, Electricians, & HVAC Technicians will send one of expert technicians to complete a skillful inspection and inform you of our findings and all the available options. How we conduct sewer line inspections A sewer line camera inspection is done by using three pieces of equipment: The rigid see-snake is an extremely durable reel-and-camera system that allows us to pinpoint problems underground. It has a flexible camera head, as well as a fiberglass-reinforced pushrod so it can execute multiple 90-degree angles and travel as far as 325 feet. Its friction-reducing design allows for maximum push with minimal effort. The camera head is also equipped with self-leveling technology, which keeps the image upright as it navigates through turns and fittings. As the snake is pushed down into the pipe, it delivers a clear, sharp image to a G-vision monitor. G-vision is a high-quality, lightweight way to monitor what is happening in your pipes. When coupled with the rigid see-snake, it is a surefire way to catch any obstructed or damaged areas that may exist underground. The monitor is mounted easily onto the camera reel and can record directly to a thumb drive, hard drive, iPhone, or iPad for later viewing. Also, an LCD screen and internal battery allows for up to four hours of full-color video inspection time that can be seen even in direct sunlight. When an internal problem is spotted on the screen, the problem area is found using a rigid locator. The rigid locator is, as it sounds, a fast and easy way to locate exactly where a see-snake has spotted an affected or compromised area. This piece of equipment is extremely helpful, as it is able to guide you down the snake line as well as measure the depth of the pipe inspection camera head. When used along with the see-snake and G-vision monitor, it allows for a quick and accurate diagnosis of pipes with no need to excavate the entire line. With these tools and technologies, Western Washington’s sewer and drain specialists are able to find and repair damages in specific areas, without having to dig up the entire pipe. If you are experiencing low water pressure, we can send out one of our expert plumbing technicians to provide you with knowledgeable leak detection service to find and remedy to the issue. Sediment Build-Up &#8211; If you are seeing sediment or rust in your water, it is probably due to your pipes aging. While this doesn’t necessarily mean your pipes are about to fail, it does signal potential future issues. Build-up in pipes or water erosion is a serious issue that should be dealt with right away. Schedule Your Sump Pump Appointment near Tacoma Today Tacoma Sump Pump Services Tacoma Sewer & Drain Services What’s the Deal With Sump Pumps? Due to the wet and soggy nature of the Western Washington area, sump pumps are commonly applied to homes. A sump pump is a mechanism used to eliminate water that has collected in a sump basin. During the winter season, when the rain is at its heaviest, it’s good to have a means of flood prevention. If you have a basement that floods regularly, or your home’s foundation is below the water table, you may need a sump pump. Sump pumps are made to send otherwise unwanted water to a location where it is no longer a problem. There are two basic kinds of sump pump installations. The pedestal variety has the motor that is mounted above the sump, making it easier to service but also more exposed and conspicuous. The other is the submersible pump, in which the motor has been mounted inside the sump, having been sealed to prevent any possible short-circuiting. The Most Common Choices for Sump Pumps: If applicable, and if you have space, choose a submersible pump. This will mean that the sump pit can be lidded. Another upside to this kind of pump is that it will reduce any noise, and prevent any detritus from falling into the pit. A tight-fitting lid will also prevent moisture from being introduced into your home, which in turn will reduce the risk of mold. Consider selecting a pump that has a cast iron core rather than a plastic one . The cast iron will help dissipate and diffuse the heat to the surrounding water, which in turn can extend the life of your pump. Choose a pump with a no-screen intake to reduce the risk of clogs. Choose a mechanical switch over a pressure switch if possible , and a solid float, so it does not become waterlogged and fail to switch off. Install a secondary pump . If you have converted your basement into usable living space, or your basement is used to store valuables, installing a secondary pump right next to the first might be a good idea. As Tacoma sewer and drain technicians, we know that installing a functioning backup pump will enable you to rest easy, knowing that your basement is safe even if the primary pump fails. Consider making your backup pump battery-operated . In the event of a power outage, a battery operated sump pump can operate functionally usually for no more than two days, though this can depend on the demand. The importance of having a sump pump in the Pacific Northwest cannot be overstated. Whether for a home or a business, a sump pump will help keep the ground from becoming unstable due to water saturation. At Harts Plumbers, Electricians, & HVAC Technicians, our team of sump pump specialists can help you identify your home’s unique needs. HEADINGS: Pipe Boring Service in Tacoma | Sewer & Drain | Pipe Boring Services | How the Pipe Boring Process Works | Explore Minimally Invasive Pipe Boring Services in Tacoma, WA | Pipe Boring and Trenchless Pipe Installation | Reviews | Offers & Discounts
Schedule Your Pipe Boring Appointment near Tacoma Today Pipe Boring Service in Tacoma Tacoma Sewer & Drain Services Pipe boring is used to install pipes under obstacles such as roads, buildings, sidewalks, or wetlands. As a leading pipe boring company in Western Washington, we have the training and experience to properly install pipes without the need to dig a trench in your yard. Depending on the size of the bore, our pipe boring experts will use one of two pieces of equipment: The basement buddy is a small drill designed to re-pipe, from the basement of a home all the way to the curb stop. This drill is able to navigate up, down, left, and right, which ensures that your new service line will be installed accurately every time. This particular tool comes equipped with a pit launch box, which allows the drill to remain stable, even in soft soil conditions. The boring machine is an extremely powerful boring drill, capable of executing a bore in most conditions. This drill creates a minimum environmental impact, so our pipe boring technicians are able to complete a bore job safely and with little to no effect on homes, businesses, or other surrounding areas. How the Pipe Boring Process Works Unsure about whether pipe boring is the right method for solving your underground piping challenge? If you’re concerned about the project’s environmental impact, accuracy of pipe placement, the duration of the job, or how much space it will take up, pipe boring checks all the boxes for speed, efficiency, and eco-friendliness. While an access area is needed to set up the direction drill used in a pipe bore, this area can be strategically placed away from homes, congestion, and businesses. Before beginning a pipe bore, our crew must carefully plan a path for drilling. This is to ensure that there will be no obstructions, such as other utility lines. Like with all trenchless repairs, a pipe bore requires both an entrance and exit pit. To begin, pipe boring technicians set up the directional at the entrance pit. The entrance pit is used to contain and manage the drilling fluids. It’s important that our crew maintains communication with each other throughout the entire process. The directional drill is tracked remotely using radio signals. These signals are used to report the depth and pitch of the drill. This allows for one to give directions to the directional drill operator, instructing them on which way to steer the drill bit. The drill can be steered in any direction making for a clean, unobstructed path. This process is known as drilling a pilot bore. After the pilot bore is dug, the resulting drill path is typically enlarged to one and a half times the pipe that is being installed. A reamer is attached and pulled back through the initial path to enlarge it. After the bore path is enlarged, the pipe can be pulled into place by the directional drill rig. Schedule Your Hydro Jetting Appointment near Tacoma Today Tacoma Hydro Jetting Experts Tacoma Sewer & Drain Services A hydro jetter utilizes several different styles of jetter heads to push 2-18 gallons of water through pipes at an estimated 4000 PSI. Depending on the size of the jetter, it can clear pipes anywhere from 1.5 to 6 inches in diameter. Using both forward- and rear-facing nozzles, the head is forced forward into the obstruction, while strong jets of water break it apart, cleaning the pipe walls through pressure washing. The jetter head is attached to a high-pressure hose, which is in turn connected to a water reservoir. The reservoir allows the jetter to be used remotely and independent from an outside water source. We use five different styles of jetter heads for various needs, including: Warthog – Can negotiate elbows and clean-outs commonly found in homes, restaurants, buildings, and other light commercial facilities. Penetrating nozzle – Features an additional forward-pointing jet that blasts a hole in solid ice or sludge blockages; three reverse jets provide propulsion. Chisel Tip Nozzle – Has multiple forward-firing jets that allow for maximum blockage penetration and debris movement. Reverse Flusher – Has three jets angled backward and to the side for flushing out debris from blocked pipes. Jet Cleaner – General-purpose nozzle that works well in most applications. Hydro jet sewer cleaning is by far the best and most effective way to get rid of stubborn clogs and tree roots that are all too common in the Pacific Northwest. Hydro jet sewer cleaning is a great option for both commercial and residential areas. Plumbing is used much more frequently in a commercial setting, and therefore, business facilities are prone to many more pipe maintenance issues. Hydro jetting can be a great preventative tool, reducing the chance of losing business and inconveniencing customers. From a residential perspective, a hydro jetter is usually your last option in trying to solve plumbing issues, before replacing either part or all of your sewer line. Cutting out roots with a hydro jetter can often buy you a year or two, giving you time to save for a complete replacement of the sewer pipes. Schedule Your Pipe Relining Appointment near Tacoma Today Tacoma Pipe Relining Experts Tacoma Sewer & Drain Services Pipe relining repair is a trenchless method that uses Cure in Place Pipe (CIPP) as a replacement for broken or damaged sewer lines. This method is used whenever conditions are deemed unfavorable or unnecessary for pipe boring or the services of a pipe bursting technician . Pipelining is a relatively new technology that has entirely revolutionized the plumbing industry. Bringing in an expert pipe relining company can save you money, time, and hassle. Lining a pipe is fast, easy, and extremely cost-effective in certain situations. THE PROCESS OF PIPE RELINING Before anything is done to install the new liner, we must first scope and locate the problem areas in your sewer line with advanced camera technology. A Ridgid Seesnake camera is sent down into your lines and monitored via a closed-circuit television monitor. This allows us to see any root intrusions, pinholes (offsets, bellying, cracks), or anything else that might contribute to sub-par performance in your pipes. In addition to scoping the pipes, we must also clean them out before we can apply a new liner. We also use our hydro-jetter . Once we have located the source of the problem, we can decide whether an excavation will be required or not. After everything is planned and cleaned out, the process begins with a felt liner. This will eventually become your new pipe. This felt pipe is saturated with resin, and the resin is pushed through using an elevated roller to be evenly distributed throughout. Once the felt is thoroughly saturated, it is wound up into a perma-liner inversion tank and oiled to reduce any friction that might occur on its way through the old pipe. Then the liner is folded back and held in place to start the inversion. Air pressure is then increased, allowing the liner to invert into the old pipeline. Not only is the liner able to negotiate 90-degree bends, but it is also able to conform to different sized pipes taking the form of the host pipe. The liner is then allowed to cure. The new pipe can then be cured with ambient air or by using either hot water or UV light. This entire process makes for a brand new pipe that is: Resistant to corrosion and lasts 50 years Harts Plumbers, Electricians, & HVAC Technicians Tacoma Stephen was a thorough expert who talked through all potential scenarios of our plumbing issue (sump pump and sewer). Schedule Your Pipe Bursting Appointment near Tacoma Today Pipe Bursting Service in Tacoma Tacoma Sewer & Drain Services Trenchless Pipe Solutions Performed by Pipe Bursting Experts The Pipe Fusion Process by Pipe Bursting Technicians Frequently, before a burst can take place, our pipe bursting technicians must first fuse several lengths of pipe to get the correct length. Pipe fusion is a simple process that involves using a heating element to melt and press two lengths of pipe together. The joint connecting the high-density polyethylene pipe, created with the pipe fuser, is stronger than the actual pipe itself. Once the correct length of pipe is achieved, the bursting head can be attached to the end. How our pipe bursting experts get the job done right: A bursting head is a semi-cone shaped tool (oftentimes with fins) that is used to break through an existing pipe. One end of it is attached to the new pipe, while the smaller end of the cone is attached to a cable that is run through the launching access hole. The unique shape and size of the bursting head, along with the hammering motion it makes, helps it break through the old pipe with ease. The bursting head is attached to the pulling cable. This cable must be strong enough to withstand being pulled through the old pipe by hydraulics. Hydraulic Power Pack and Burster The hydraulic power pack is used to pull the cable, and consequently the bursting head. It is designed to pull the head in a hammering motion. This process will break up the original pipe to make way for the new one. Pipe Bursting Preparation Procedure Tim Paulk, our Lead Excavation Tech at Harts Plumbing explains the bursting preparation protocol for uncovering a main sewer pipe. Pipe bursting is a trenchless method of replacing buried pipelines (such as sewer, water, or natural-gas pipes) without the need for a traditional construction trench. “Launching and receiving pits” replace the trench needed by conventional pipe-laying. Stay Code Compliant With a Surge Protector Electrical Safety Inspections You Can Rely On How Does a Whole House Surge Protector Work? Whole house surge protectors are heroes in the realm of electrical safety. They function by monitoring the flow of electricity into our homes. When they detect an excess voltage that surpasses a safe threshold — typically caused by power surges — they divert the extra electricity to the ground wire. This immediate action protects our home&#8217;s electrical systems and the myriad of devices connected to them. The installation of a whole house surge protection device involves integrating it with your main breaker panel. This strategic position allows it to serve as the first line of defense against power surges, ensuring that only the electricity needed is distributed throughout your home. The effectiveness of these devices is measured in their voltage protection rating, a key factor to consider when choosing the right protector for your home. How the Pipe Boring Process Works Unsure about whether pipe boring is the right method for solving your underground piping challenge? Before beginning a pipe bore, our crew must carefully plan a path for drilling. This is to ensure that there will be no obstructions, such as other utility lines. Like with all trenchless repairs, a pipe bore requires both an entrance and exit pit. To begin, pipe boring technicians set up the directional at the entrance pit. The entrance pit is used to contain and manage the drilling fluids. It’s important that our crew maintains communication with each other throughout the entire process. The directional drill is tracked remotely using radio signals. These signals are used to report the depth and pitch of the drill. This allows for one to give directions to the directional drill operator, instructing them on which way to steer the drill bit. After the pilot bore is dug, the resulting drill path is typically enlarged to one and a half times the pipe that is being installed. A reamer is attached and pulled back through the initial path to enlarge it. After the bore path is enlarged, the pipe can be pulled into place by the directional drill rig. Homeowners in Renton often have questions about sewer repair , especially when backups, odors, or slow drains start affecting daily life. Below are answers to some of the most common questions we hear, so you can better understand what&rsquo;s happening and when it&rsquo;s time to schedule professional service. Does Renton’s "glacial till" soil affect my sewer pipes? Yes, significantly. Many Renton neighborhoods—especially those on the hills like Kennydale or West Hill —sit on &#8220;glacial till,&#8221; a dense, rocky soil that shifts with Washington’s heavy rains. This shifting can cause older clay or cast iron pipes to &#8220;offset&#8221; or crack. In lower-lying areas near the Cedar River , the soil is more sandy and prone to erosion, which can lead to &#8220;pipe sagging&#8221; (bellies) where waste settles and causes frequent backups. What kind of sewer pipes does my home near Liberty Park have? If your home was built between the 1920s and 1960s (common in North Renton and near the downtown core), you likely have clay tile or cast iron pipes. While durable, clay is highly susceptible to root intrusion from Renton’s mature Douglas firs and maples. If your home was built in the mid-century boom, you might even have Orangeburg (tar paper) pipes , which are known to collapse under the pressure of our local wet soil and require immediate replacement. Do I need a permit from the City of Renton for trenchless sewer repair? Yes. The City of Renton requires a Utility Permit for any repair, alteration, or replacement of a side sewer. If the repair extends into the public right-of-way (like under a Renton sidewalk), a Civil Construction Permit and a Traffic Control Plan may also be required. Harts Plumbers, Electricians, & HVAC Technicians handles the entire Renton permitting process for you, ensuring your repair is up to the latest City of Renton code. How do Renton’s mature trees affect my sewer system? Renton is known for its beautiful &#8220;Canopy Cover,&#8221; but those roots are the #1 cause of sewer blockages here. Roots from large trees in neighborhoods like Skyway or Briarwood seek out the moisture inside your pipes. Once they find a tiny crack or a loose joint in an old clay pipe, they grow inside, creating a &#8220;root ball&#8221; that acts like a filter, catching grease and paper until the line is completely blocked. Is trenchless "no-dig" sewer repair possible in Renton’s hilly terrain? Absolutely. In fact, trenchless repair is often the best choice for Renton’s topography. Because many homes in the Highlands or Talbot Hill have steep driveways or complex landscaping, traditional digging can be incredibly destructive and expensive. We use pipe bursting or CIPP (Cured-In-Place Pipe) lining to fix your sewer without tearing up your yard or ruining your view of the valley. I received a notice about a "Sanitary Sewer Overflow" (SSO). What does this mean? If sewage is backing up into your yard or onto the street, the City of Renton considers it an illegal health hazard (SSO). You are typically given a strict timeframe to fix the issue. Because Renton treats its wastewater at the South Treatment Plant (King County) , the city is very proactive about preventing leaks that could contaminate the Cedar River or Lake Washington . Call us immediately if you see wastewater seeping—we offer 24/7 emergency response for Renton residents. Why is my Renton sewer bill so high, and can a repair help? Your bill includes a King County Sewer Capacity Charge and City of Renton usage fees. If you have &#8220;Inflow and Infiltration&#8221; (I&I)—where rainwater from your gutters or cracked pipes leaks into the sewer system—it can sometimes lead to higher costs or system strain. Fixing a cracked side sewer ensures you aren&#8217;t sending &#8220;clean&#8221; groundwater to the treatment plant, which helps the environment and prevents your line from being overwhelmed during Renton’s rainy season. What are the rules for sewer repairs near the Cedar River or Lake Washington? Renton has strict Shoreline Master Program (SMP) and Critical Areas Ordinance regulations. If your property is within 200 feet of the Cedar River , Lake Washington , or the Black River , your sewer repair may require a Shoreline Exemption or a special Critical Areas review. The city is particularly protective of these zones to prevent untreated wastewater from entering salmon habitats. How we conduct sewer line inspections A sewer line camera inspection is done by using three pieces of equipment: The rigid see-snake is an extremely durable reel-and-camera system that allows us to pinpoint problems underground. It has a flexible camera head, as well as a fiberglass-reinforced pushrod so it can execute multiple 90-degree angles and travel as far as 325 feet. Its friction-reducing design allows for maximum push with minimal effort. The camera head is also equipped with self-leveling technology, which keeps the image upright as it navigates through turns and fittings. As the snake is pushed down into the pipe, it delivers a clear, sharp image to a G-vision monitor. G-vision is a high-quality, lightweight way to monitor what is happening in your pipes. When coupled with the rigid see-snake, it is a surefire way to catch any obstructed or damaged areas that may exist underground. The monitor is mounted easily onto the camera reel and can record directly to a thumb drive, hard drive, iPhone, or iPad for later viewing. Also, an LCD screen and internal battery allows for up to four hours of full-color video inspection time that can be seen even in direct sunlight. When an internal problem is spotted on the screen, the problem area is found using a rigid locator. The rigid locator is, as it sounds, a fast and easy way to locate exactly where a see-snake has spotted an affected or compromised area. This piece of equipment is extremely helpful, as it is able to guide you down the snake line as well as measure the depth of the pipe inspection camera head. When used along with the see-snake and G-vision monitor, it allows for a quick and accurate diagnosis of pipes with no need to excavate the entire line. With these tools and technologies, Western Washington’s sewer and drain specialists are able to find and repair damages in specific areas, without having to dig up the entire pipe. We Service and Install Several Different Kinds of Water Heaters As veteran technicians, we take pride in our ability to service any type of water heaters with ease. No matter which one you prefer for your home, our Seattle plumbers are always available to help you install, maintain, or repair your water heater. The residential water heater types we install include: Conventional Storage Water Heaters: The most popular type of home water heating system. A single-family storage heater can hold anywhere from 20 to 80 gallons of hot water. The fuel source of these water heaters vary and can include natural gas, propane, fuel oil, or electricity. A conventional storage water heater installation is both fast and cost-effective! Heat Pump Water Heaters: These types of water heaters use electricity to move heat from one place to another instead of heating directly. Somewhat like a refrigerator in reverse, heat pump water heaters pull heat from the air surrounding it and dump it at a higher temperature into the tank in order to heat water. Because heat pumps work this way, they operate more efficiently in warm climates. Solar Water Heaters: Using solar energy from the sun to generate heat, hot water automatically rises into the tank. Just like your conventional water heater, solar water heaters have a storage tank that is mounted above a set of solar panels on the roof. During the colder season, you may need an automatic or electric backup to heat the water. Tankless Coil and Indirect Water Heaters: These types of water heaters forego the usual storage, creating hot water on demand. Using the heating coil or heat exchanger installed in the main furnace or boiler, hot water is heated with just the turn of a faucet. These systems work best in colder climates or during the winter when heating systems are used regularly. Ready to upgrade? Reach out to Seattle&#8217;s water heater installation experts at Harts Plumbers, Electricians, & HVAC Technicians today! We&#8217;re dedicated to finding the perfect unit for your home so you never run into hot water issues again.
